---
title: "Between-participant designs"
execute:
  cache: false
---

ManyBabies 1 combines two condition structures. Speech register varies [within infant](within-participant-designs.qmd), while the four pseudorandom trial orders vary between infants. One infant is associated with one order across all sixteen possible test-trial rows.

```{r}
manybabies <- readRDS("data/manybabies/manybabies1-trials.rds")

stopifnot(
  nrow(manybabies) == 37264L,
  length(unique(manybabies$infant_id)) == 2329L,
  all(table(manybabies$infant_id) == 16L)
)

order_by_infant <- vapply(
  split(manybabies$counterbalance_order, manybabies$infant_id),
  function(x) {
    observed <- unique(stats::na.omit(x))
    stopifnot(length(observed) == 1L)
    as.integer(observed)
  },
  integer(1)
)

infants <- manybabies[
  !duplicated(manybabies$infant_id),
  c("infant_id", "lab_id")
]
infants$assigned_order <- unname(order_by_infant[infants$infant_id])
stopifnot(length(unique(infants$assigned_order)) == 4L)
```

In a [**between-participant design**](https://opentextbc.ca/researchmethods/chapter/experimental-design/), each participant contributes observations to only one level of a factor. The factor comparison is across groups rather than within the same participant.

## A group contrast over assigned order

Let $Y_i$ be infant $i$'s mean log looking time over included trials, and let $Z_i$ identify the infant's assigned order. The mean in order group $z$ is

$$
\overline Y_z=\frac{1}{n_z}\sum_{i:Z_i=z}Y_i.
$$

Each infant contributes to one and only one $overline Y_z$. Stable infant differences do not cancel through within-infant subtraction. This is the defining contrast with the IDS-minus-ADS summary on the preceding page.

We construct $Y_i$ from the included looking times and then join the infant's single order label.

```{r}
observed <- manybabies[!manybabies$trial_missing, ]

infant_mean_log <- aggregate(
  log(looking_time_seconds) ~ infant_id,
  data = observed,
  FUN = mean
)
names(infant_mean_log)[2L] <- "mean_log_looking_time"

between_data <- merge(
  infants,
  infant_mean_log,
  by = "infant_id",
  all.x = TRUE
)

between_summary <- aggregate(
  mean_log_looking_time ~ assigned_order,
  data = between_data,
  FUN = function(x) c(
    infants = length(x),
    mean = mean(x),
    sd = stats::sd(x)
  )
)

between_summary <- data.frame(
  assigned_order = between_summary$assigned_order,
  infants_with_outcome = as.integer(
    between_summary$mean_log_looking_time[, "infants"]
  ),
  mean_log_looking_time = between_summary$mean_log_looking_time[, "mean"],
  sd_log_looking_time = between_summary$mean_log_looking_time[, "sd"]
)

knitr::kable(
  between_summary,
  digits = 3,
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

Among infants with an included outcome, the four groups contain `r paste(format(between_summary$infants_with_outcome, big.mark = ","), collapse = ", ")` infants. Their mean log looking times are `r paste(sprintf("%.3f", between_summary$mean_log_looking_time), collapse = ", ")`. The raw infant summaries and group means show the scale of between-infant variation.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 5.8
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-alt: "Infant mean log looking times in each assigned trial-order group, with group means marked."

ggplot2::ggplot(
  between_data[!is.na(between_data$mean_log_looking_time), ],
  ggplot2::aes(x = factor(assigned_order), y = mean_log_looking_time)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter(
    width = 0.16,
    height = 0,
    alpha = 0.18, # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting
    size = 0.8,
    color = "grey25"
  ) +
  ggplot2::stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    color = "#2C6E9B",
    size = 2.2
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Assigned order",
    y = "Infant mean log looking time"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 11)
```

## Order is a nuisance assignment

This plot does not estimate a linguistic treatment effect. Trial order was used to distribute register and paired stimulus identity over session position. It is a between-infant factor, but it is not the speech-register contrast that motivated the experiment.

The documented evidence about allocation also limits interpretation. Because the public source does not specify each laboratory's infant-to-order allocation device, differences among these four realized groups are descriptive. They should not be labeled causal effects of order.

## Trials improve an infant summary, not group replication

The release contains `r format(nrow(observed), big.mark = ",")` included trial outcomes from `r format(nrow(infant_mean_log), big.mark = ",")` infants. More included trials may make an infant's $Y_i$ less sensitive to a particular stimulus. They do not increase $n_z$, because order was attached once to the infant.

A trial-weighted group mean would give more influence to infants with more included trials. The displayed analysis instead gives every infant with an outcome one group-level contribution. This choice matches the between-infant comparison in the equation, though the figure remains descriptive.

## An observed laboratory attribute is not an assigned factor

Testing method also differs across infants, but laboratories used their established head-turn preference, single-screen, or eye-tracking procedures. Method is partly tied to laboratory and was not assigned to infants. It is thus not interchangeable with the assigned order factor. A difference among method groups may combine method, laboratory, infant population, age coverage, and local implementation.

::: {.callout-note title="Audit the between-infant comparison"}
1. Why does each infant enter only one order-group mean?
2. What does averaging trials within infant preserve about the assignment unit?
3. Why is assigned order a nuisance factor rather than the linguistic treatment?
4. Why can testing method not be analyzed as if it had been randomly assigned?
:::

A between-participant design compares groups whose members occupy only one factor level. In ManyBabies 1, order has this structure, whereas register does not. The next page checks how the four orders [counterbalance register and paired stimuli](counterbalancing.qmd).
